claims.title: README says gatewayToken is copied but deploy.sh/key naming not verified in docs; gateway token piped without empty check
claims.text:
🟡 **P2**

**README says gatewayToken is copied but deploy.sh/key naming not verified in docs; gateway token piped without empty check**

If the `stealth-browser-secrets` Secret lacks `.data.gatewayToken` (or the secret doesn't exist yet), jsonpath yields empty output and `base64 -d` outputs nothing. Because of `pipefail`, a missing secret errors out, but a missing key produces an empty stream. `kubectl create secret --from-file=token=/dev/stdin` then creates `searxng-gateway` with an empty token and applies it without error. The engine will then send an empty bearer token and fail with auth errors at search time, while the rollout reports success. Capture the token into a variable and fail if it is empty.

<!-- ai-review:fp=bug|deploy/k8s/searxng/deploy.sh|690ee011082cc509.0 -->

claims.title: Gateway token copy fails silently into an empty Secret
claims.text:
🟡 **P2**

**Gateway token copy fails silently into an empty Secret**

With `pipefail`, a missing `stealth-browser-secrets` Secret or `gatewayToken` key aborts the script. But if the Secret exists and the key is absent, the jsonpath returns an empty string. `base64 -d` then succeeds on empty input, and `--from-file=token=/dev/stdin` creates or overwrites `searxng-gateway` with an empty token. The script continues without any error. The engine then sends unauthenticated requests to the gateway and every `gg` search fails at runtime with a 401. Capture the token into a variable and fail with a clear message if it is empty. This is the same fail-fast check that the Brave key file option already has.

<!-- ai-review:fp=bug|deploy/k8s/searxng/deploy.sh|690ee011082cc509.0 -->

claims.title: README says gatewayToken, but nothing documents the key is required
claims.text:
🟡 **P2**

**README says gatewayToken, but nothing documents the key is required**

deploy.sh pipes `jq`-less jsonpath `{.data.gatewayToken}` through `base64 -d`. If the Secret or key is absent, jsonpath yields empty output, and with `set -o pipefail` only kubectl's exit status matters (a missing key still exits 0). The script then creates `searxng-gateway` with an empty token and proceeds, so the engine would be deployed with an empty STEALTH_BROWSER_TOKEN and fail with auth errors at search time. Add a non-empty check before creating the Secret.

<!-- ai-review:fp=bug|deploy/k8s/searxng/deploy.sh|690ee011082cc509.0 -->

claims.title: README says deploy.sh copies `gatewayToken` but omits the stale/accurate wording on restart; also doc omits Reloader dependency
claims.text:
🟢 **P3**

**README says deploy.sh copies `gatewayToken` but omits the stale/accurate wording on restart; also doc omits Reloader dependency**

The README bullet says deploy.sh copies `gatewayToken` into `searxng-gateway`, which matches the script. However, the Deployment relies on `reloader.stakater.com/auto`, and `deploy.sh` comments note that Reloader skips newly created Secrets. The gateway-token Secret is re-applied on every run but `rollout restart` only occurs when `--brave-key-file` is passed. A rotated gateway token therefore depends on Reloader being installed, which the docs do not mention.

<!-- ai-review:fp=nitpick|deploy/k8s/searxng/deploy.sh|502c0e7e614e4fae.0 -->

claims.title: Gateway token sent over plaintext HTTP with no NetworkPolicy
claims.text:
🟢 **P3**

**Gateway token sent over plaintext HTTP with no NetworkPolicy**

The gateway bearer token reaches the gateway via `http://` inside the cluster, so the token is unencrypted on the pod network. No NetworkPolicy in these manifests limits who can reach the gateway or who can sniff this traffic. This is defense-in-depth rather than an exploit, so consider TLS or a mesh, or at least a NetworkPolicy restricting ingress to the gateway from the `searxng` namespace.

<!-- ai-review:fp=security|deploy/k8s/searxng/deployment.yaml|adb60f490d8b3346.0 -->

claims.title: README says deploy.sh copies `gatewayToken` but omits the key rename and describes a different flow
claims.text:
🟢 **P3**

**README says deploy.sh copies `gatewayToken` but omits the key rename and describes a different flow**

The Deployment mounts the gateway token with no NetworkPolicy shown, and the token travels in plain HTTP to the gateway (`http://gateway...:8080`). This is intra-cluster, so low risk, but the bearer token is unencrypted on the pod network. Consider documenting or restricting access with a NetworkPolicy.
